front.title: The SNAC Router Flag in ICMPv6 Router Advertisement Messages

abstract.t: This document defines a new flag, the SNAC Router flag, in the Router Advertisement message that can be used to distinguish configuration information sent by Stub Network Auto-Configuring (SNAC) routers from information sent by transit routers.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Per , networks can either be transit or stub networks. Transit networks are those capable of carrying data traffic that is neither locally originated nor locally destined.

A Stub Network Auto-Configuring (SNAC) router is an autonomously configuring router that provides IP connectivity between one or more stub networks and one or more transit networks. A common example of a SNAC router is a device that attaches a 6LoWPAN-based network to a home network, automatically providing IPv6 forwarding between the two networks without explicit operator configuration. This document defines a new IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Router Advertisement (RA) flag, the SNAC Router flag, which SNAC routers use to identify RAs sent by other SNAC routers.
Readers can refer to for an overview of a set of practices for automatically connecting IPv6 stub networks to transit networks.

section.name: SNAC Router Flag
section.t: The SNAC Router flag is bit 6 in the RA Flags Extension Option .

The SNAC Router flag bit with a value of '1' is reserved for use by SNAC routers. Receipt of an RA with that bit set to '1' indicates that the sending router is a SNAC router. Describing the exact triggers when a SNAC router sets this flag to '1' is out of scope for this document. An example of such considerations is documented in .

Consistent with , devices that do not operate as SNAC routers will not set the SNAC Router flag bit to '1', and devices that do not understand the SNAC Router flag will silently ignore it. This means that setting the flag bit to '1' or '0' should not change the behavior of such devices in any way (other than that it is permissible to log and cache the value of the flag bit as part of normal router advertisement processing, where applicable).

section.name: Operational Considerations
section.t: In environments that implement RA-Guard in a way that filters RAs sent by SNAC routers, devices on the transit network will never receive an RA with the SNAC Router flag bit set to '1'.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: How SNAC routers process RAs is dependent on the SNAC Router flag value.
The security considerations of IPv6 Neighbor Discovery are documented in Section Security Considerations of . The addition of the SNAC Router flag does not change these considerations.
